stalenessRisksFound.description: A structural-parsing algorithm change (STRUCTURAL_INDEX_VERSION bump or any parseDocumentStructure fix) over unchanged document text is invisible to orchestrator.ts's STRUCTURE-stage cache gate; getOrRunStage silently resumes and re-persists the pre-change structural nodes.

orchestrator.ts's AMENDMENTS-stage cache gate is keyed only on document label, not text, while the real stage function also inspects text — a text edit that flips amendment-shaped detection is not recompiled.

persistence.ts's upsert functions never delete a previously-persisted row for content the current run no longer produces; orphaned DocumentNode/DefinedTermNode/ContractRule rows survive indefinitely and are returned by plain reads (e.g. service.ts's findMany by documentId) alongside current rows.

coverage-audit/pipeline.ts hardcodes a stale structuralParserVersion literal ("phase-2a-structural-index") into its own content-identity fingerprint instead of importing the real, current STRUCTURAL_INDEX_VERSION constant — already visibly wrong today (types.ts now defines "phase-3f1-2-structural-identity.v1"); this field cannot currently detect a structural-parser-version change at all.

The legacy Phase C compiler's own dangerous-unflagged safety gap (25.0% then 15.625%, both above its required ≤5% gate) was never closed and remains in still-present, unmodified code (RULE_EXTRACTION/VERIFICATION/PROMOTION stages); combined with the STRUCTURE/AMENDMENTS cache-gate defects above, any future re-run of this pipeline against a real package risks silently compounding stale/incorrect structural input on top of an already-known-unsafe extraction path.
